summary: End-to-end testing of Stripe Connect (Express) integration for driver payouts. Backend: 16/16 pytest PASSED in /app/backend/tests/test_stripe_connect.py — covers RBAC on all 3 /driver/connect/* endpoints, empty-status shape, onboard (creates real Stripe Express account with country=CA + card_payments/transfers capabilities, persists stripe_account_id, returns stripe.com account_link URL), onboard idempotency (reuses existing stripe_account_id, returns fresh URL), status post-onboard (connected:true, charges_enabled:false as expected for unfinished hosted flow, requirements.currently_due present), login-link 400 before + accepts 200/400 after, tip-flow fallback when charges_enabled=false (routed_to_driver:false, payment_transactions.connect_routed:false), Connect-routed code path with fake acct_ (returns 400 Stripe error as expected), tip fallback with no account, plus regression (admin/stats, driver/balance, permits/list, driver/tips shape). Frontend: Playwright verified 3 UI states on /billing — (1) unconnected → 'Not Connected' grey badge + 'Connect Stripe' button triggers POST /driver/connect/onboard, (2) connected-but-incomplete → amber 'Onboarding Incomplete' badge + 'Finish Onboarding' button, (3) charges_enabled=true (mocked via route intercept) → green 'Active' badge + 'Stripe Dashboard' button that calls POST /driver/connect/login-link and invokes window.open(stripeUrl, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer'). ?stripe_return=1 shows 'Stripe onboarding complete' toast and strips the param. All 3 test Express accounts deleted via stripe.Account.delete; driver1 restored to unconnected state. No bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1271 lines (>>700 threshold). Connect endpoints, tip checkout, job CRUD, admin, permits, commission ledger are all in one file. Strongly recommend splitting into routers/connect.py, routers/tips.py, routers/payments.py, routers/jobs.py, routers/admin.py.

server.py get_connect_status (L806-842): on every call, synchronously calls stripe.Account.retrieve and writes charges_enabled/payouts_enabled/details_submitted into mongo. This is correct for source-of-truth, but it's a stripe API call on every /billing page load. Consider caching for ~30s or switching to a webhook-driven sync (account.updated event).

server.py create_tip_checkout (L620-720): 'use_connect' branch reads driver.stripe_account_id + driver.stripe_charges_enabled from mongo (which can lag reality). Status endpoint re-syncs on each call, but tip endpoint does not. If a driver's Stripe account is later disabled, the tip endpoint could still attempt destination charge and return 400. Acceptable — Stripe will reject — but consider surfacing 'payouts paused' message to tipper instead of raw Stripe error.
BillingPage.js (L42): GET /driver/connect/status is called on every mount. On slow connections this serializes with the other 3 parallel calls and can add noticeable latency. Minor.
BillingPage.js (L63): `window.location.href = r.data.url` — consider using window.location.assign for better back-button semantics.

server.py start_connect_onboarding (L764-804): catches stripe.error.StripeError only; if the DB update_one fails after a successful Stripe account creation, a new Account exists in Stripe but not persisted locally → next onboarding call creates a duplicate. Consider wrapping in try/except with Stripe.Account.delete rollback, or creating the DB record first with a placeholder then patching.
